cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: The U.S. funds for which The Vanguard Group, Inc. (VGI) acts as investment advisor (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Board of Trustees for each of the Vanguard-advised funds has adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. Vanguard's Investment Stewardship Team administers the day-to-day operation of the funds' proxy voting process, overseen by the Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice pilots are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit about.vanguard.com/investment-stewardship.The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX by VGI were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, VGI's voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. Votes contained in this report include votes made by unaffiliated third-party investment advisors (External Advisors) who exercised voting power over some or all of the securities voted. Votes made by the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Board of Trustees for each of the Vanguard-advised funds has adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. Vanguard's Investment Stewardship Team administers the day-to-day operation of the funds' proxy voting process, overseen by the Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice pilots are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit about.vanguard.com/investment-stewardship.The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX by VGI were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, VGI's voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. Votes contained in this report include votes made by unaffiliated third-party investment advisors (External Advisors) who exercised voting power over some or all of the securities voted. Votes made by the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: On January 12, 2026, The Vanguard Group, Inc. ("VGI") and its affiliates (together, "Vanguard") completed an internal reorganization of portfolio management functions for the U.S. Vanguard funds into two wholly owned U.S. investment advisors, Vanguard Capital Management, LLC ("VCM") and Vanguard Portfolio Management, LLC ("VPM") (the "Internal Reorganization"). Each of these investment advisors consists of distinct investment management teams and investment stewardship teams with proxy voting administrative responsibilities. As of the effective date of the Internal Reorganization, VCM and VPM began exercising investment discretion and providing proxy voting administrative services for the funds to which they provide portfolio management services. The U.S. funds for which VGI acts as investment advisor through VCM and VPM (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Investment Committees of the Board of Trustees for the Vanguard-advised funds have adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. The Vanguard Capital Management Investment Stewardship Team and Vanguard Portfolio Management Investment Stewardship Team administer the day-to-day operations of the proxy voting process of the funds managed by VCM and VPM, respectively, as overseen by the relevant Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee appointed by each Investment Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice program are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders under Vanguard's Investor Choice program. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit Proxy voting across Vanguard funds | Vanguard. The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, the voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI, VCM or VPM or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. In addition, votes contained in this report include votes made by unaffiliated third-party investment advisors (External Advisors) who exercised voting power overs some or all of the securities voted. Votes made by VGI, VCM or VPM, or the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: The U.S. funds for which The Vanguard Group, Inc. (VGI) acts as investment advisor (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, The Board of Trustees for each of the Vanguard-advised funds has adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. Vanguard's Investment Stewardship Team administers the day-to-day operation of the funds' proxy voting process, overseen by the Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice pilots are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit about.vanguard.com/investment-stewardship.The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX by VGI were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, VGI's voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. Votes contained in this report include votes made by unaffiliated third-party investment advisors (External Advisors) who exercised voting power over some or all of the securities voted. Votes made by the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Board of Trustees for each of the Vanguard-advised funds has adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. Vanguard's Investment Stewardship Team administers the day-to-day operation of the funds' proxy voting process, overseen by the Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice pilots are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit about.vanguard.com/investment-stewardship.The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX by VGI were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, VGI's voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: On January 12, 2026, The Vanguard Group, Inc. ("VGI") and its affiliates (together, "Vanguard") completed an internal reorganization of portfolio management functions for the U.S. Vanguard funds into two wholly owned U.S. investment advisors, Vanguard Capital Management, LLC ("VCM") and Vanguard Portfolio Management, LLC ("VPM") (the "Internal Reorganization"). Each of these investment advisors consists of distinct investment management teams and investment stewardship teams with proxy voting administrative responsibilities. As of the effective date of the Internal Reorganization, VCM and VPM began exercising investment discretion and providing proxy voting administrative services for the funds to which they provide portfolio management services. The U.S. funds for which VGI acts as investment advisor through VCM and VPM (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Investment Committees of the Board of Trustees for the Vanguard-advised funds have adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. The Vanguard Capital Management Investment Stewardship Team and Vanguard Portfolio Management Investment Stewardship Team administer the day-to-day operations of the proxy voting process of the funds managed by VCM and VPM, respectively, as overseen by the relevant Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee appointed by each Investment Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice program are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders under Vanguard's Investor Choice program. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit Proxy voting across Vanguard funds | Vanguard. The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, the voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI, VCM or VPM or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. In addition, votes contained in this report include votes made by unaffiliated third-party investment advisors (External Advisors) who exercised voting power overs some or all of the securities voted. Votes made by VGI, VCM or VPM, or the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing.The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: A Fund does not have the right to vote proxies for securities on loans over a record date of such proxies. However, if a Funds Adviser has notice of the proxy in advance of the record date, the Funds Adviser may terminate a loan in advance of the record date if the Funds Adviser determines the vote is considered material with respect to an investment, such as when the Funds Adviser believes that its participation in the vote is necessary to preserve the long-term value of the Funds investment or in highly contested issues for which the Funds Adviser believes its vote is important to the Funds strategy. In determining whether a vote is material, the Advisers determination is informed by its responsibility to act in a Funds best interests. In most cases, the Adviser anticipates that the potential long-term value to a Fund of voting shares would not be material and would therefore not justify forgoing the potential revenue the loan may provide the Fund. This may result in proxies being voted by the borrower of the security in a way that would be contrary to how the Funds Adviser would vote if the security had not been lent. However, in certain instances, the Adviser may determine, in its independent business judgment, that the value of voting outweighs the securities lending revenue loss to a Fund and may therefore recall shares to be voted in those instances.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: Date of reporting period: July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024 A Fund does not have the right to vote proxies for securities on loans over a record date of such proxies. However, if a Fund's Adviser has notice of the proxy in advance of the record date, the Fund's Adviser may terminate a loan in advance of the record date if the Fund's Adviser determines the vote is considered material with respect to an investment, such as when the Fund's Adviser believes that its participation in the vote is necessary to preserve the long-term value of the Fund's investment or in highly contested issues for which the Fund's Adviser believes its vote is important to the Fund's strategy. In determining whether a vote is material, the Adviser's determination is informed by its responsibility to act in a Fund's best interests. In most cases, the Adviser anticipates that the potential long-term value to a Fund of voting shares would not be material and would therefore not justify forgoing the potential revenue the loan may provide the Fund. This may result in proxies being voted by the borrower of the security in a way that would be contrary to how the Fund's Adviser would vote if the security had not been lent, including for certain Funds that have strategies to invest in companies that the Fund's Adviser believes are sustainable leaders based on the Adviser's sustainability criteria or that meet certain other Environmental, Social, or Governance (ESG) criteria. However, in certain instances, the Adviser may determine, in its independent business judgment, that the value of voting outweighs the securities lending revenue loss to a Fund and may therefore recall shares to be voted in those instances.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: The U.S. funds for which The Vanguard Group, Inc. (VGI) acts as investment advisor (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, The Board of Trustees for each of the Vanguard-advised funds has adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. Vanguard's Investment Stewardship Team administers the day-to-day operation of the funds' proxy voting process, overseen by the Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice pilots are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit about.vanguard.com/investment-stewardship.The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX by VGI were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, VGI's voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. Votes contained in this report include votes made by unaffiliated third-party investment advisors (External Advisors) who exercised voting power over some or all of the securities voted. Votes made by the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: On January 12, 2026, The Vanguard Group, Inc. ("VGI") and its affiliates (together, "Vanguard") completed an internal reorganization of portfolio management functions for the U.S. Vanguard funds into two wholly owned U.S. investment advisors, Vanguard Capital Management, LLC ("VCM") and Vanguard Portfolio Management, LLC ("VPM") (the "Internal Reorganization"). Each of these investment advisors consists of distinct investment management teams and investment stewardship teams with proxy voting administrative responsibilities. As of the effective date of the Internal Reorganization, VCM and VPM began exercising investment discretion and providing proxy voting administrative services for the funds to which they provide portfolio management services. The U.S. funds for which VGI acts as investment advisor through VCM and VPM (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Investment Committees of the Board of Trustees for the Vanguard-advised funds have adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. The Vanguard Capital Management Investment Stewardship Team and Vanguard Portfolio Management Investment Stewardship Team administer the day-to-day operations of the proxy voting process of the funds managed by VCM and VPM, respectively, as overseen by the relevant Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee appointed by each Investment Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice program are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders under Vanguard's Investor Choice program. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit Proxy voting across Vanguard funds | Vanguard. The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, the voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI, VCM or VPM or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. Votes made by VGI, VCM or VPM, or the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing.The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

("VGI") and its affiliates (together, "Vanguard") completed an internal reorganization of portfolio management functions for the U.S. Vanguard funds into two wholly owned U.S. investment advisors, Vanguard Capital Management, LLC ("VCM") and Vanguard Portfolio Management, LLC ("VPM") (the "Internal Reorganization"). Each of these investment advisors consists of distinct investment management teams and investment stewardship teams with proxy voting administrative responsibilities. As of the effective date of the Internal Reorganization, VCM and VPM began exercising investment discretion and providing proxy voting administrative services for the funds to which they provide portfolio management services. The U.S. funds for which VGI acts as investment advisor through VCM and VPM (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Investment Committees of the Board of Trustees for the Vanguard-advised funds have adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. The Vanguard Capital Management Investment Stewardship Team and Vanguard Portfolio Management Investment Stewardship Team administer the day-to-day operations of the proxy voting process of the funds managed by VCM and VPM, respectively, as overseen by the relevant Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee appointed by each Investment Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice program are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders under Vanguard's Investor Choice program. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit Proxy voting across Vanguard funds | Vanguard. The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, the voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI, VCM or VPM or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. Votes made by VGI, VCM or VPM, or the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing.The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: The U.S. funds for which The Vanguard Group, Inc. (VGI) acts as investment advisor (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, The Board of Trustees for each of the Vanguard-advised funds has adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. Vanguard's Investment Stewardship Team administers the day-to-day operation of the funds' proxy voting process, overseen by the Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice pilots are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit about.vanguard.com/investment-stewardship.The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX by VGI were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, VGI's voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. Votes contained in this report include votes made by unaffiliated third-party investment advisors (External Advisors) who exercised voting power over some or all of the securities voted. Votes made by the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: The U.S. funds for which The Vanguard Group, Inc. (VGI) acts as investment advisor (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Board of Trustees for each of the Vanguard-advised funds has adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. Vanguard's Investment Stewardship Team administers the day-to-day operation of the funds' proxy voting process, overseen by the Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice pilots are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit about.vanguard.com/investment-stewardship.The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX by VGI were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, VGI's voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: During the reporting period, the MFS Conservative Allocation Portfolio, the MFS Growth Allocation Portfolio, and the MFS Moderate Allocation Portfolio, each a series of the Registrant (collectively, the "top tier funds") voted at the November 14, 2024 shareholder meetings of certain other investment companies registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended, and sponsored by MFS (each, an "Underlying MFS Fund" and collectively, the "Underlying MFS Funds"). To address any potential conflicts of interest on the part of MFS that could arise from MFS voting shares of the MFS Underlying Funds on behalf of the top tier funds, MFS voted these Underlying MFS Fund shares in the same proportion as the other shareholders of the respective MFS Underlying Fund. Additionally, the top tier funds voted at the June 18, 2025 meeting of the MFS Growth Series, a series of MFS Variable Insurance Trust and MFS voted these shares in the same manner as described above (i.e., "mirror voting"). As a result, the voting record for these meetings will reflect a split vote. Columns 10 and 12 for an underlying fund reflect dollars of net asset value. Due to rounding the amounts in Column 12 may not total the amount in Column 10. cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: On January 12, 2026, The Vanguard Group, Inc. ("VGI") and its affiliates (together, "Vanguard") completed an internal reorganization of portfolio management functions for the U.S. Vanguard funds into two wholly owned U.S. investment advisors, Vanguard Capital Management, LLC ("VCM") and Vanguard Portfolio Management, LLC ("VPM") (the "Internal Reorganization"). Each of these investment advisors consists of distinct investment management teams and investment stewardship teams with proxy voting administrative responsibilities. As of the effective date of the Internal Reorganization, VCM and VPM began exercising investment discretion and providing proxy voting administrative services for the funds to which they provide portfolio management services. The U.S. funds for which VGI acts as investment advisor through VCM and VPM (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Investment Committees of the Board of Trustees for the Vanguard-advised funds have adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. The Vanguard Capital Management Investment Stewardship Team and Vanguard Portfolio Management Investment Stewardship Team administer the day-to-day operations of the proxy voting process of the funds managed by VCM and VPM, respectively, as overseen by the relevant Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee appointed by each Investment Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice program are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders under Vanguard's Investor Choice program. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit Proxy voting across Vanguard funds | Vanguard. The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, the voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI, VCM or VPM or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. In addition, votes contained in this report include votes made by unaffiliated third-party investment advisors (External Advisors) who exercised voting power overs some or all of the securities voted. Votes made by VGI, VCM or VPM, or the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing.The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

("VGI") and its affiliates (together, "Vanguard") completed an internal reorganization of portfolio management functions for the U.S. Vanguard funds into two wholly owned U.S. investment advisors, Vanguard Capital Management, LLC ("VCM") and Vanguard Portfolio Management, LLC ("VPM") (the "Internal Reorganization"). Each of these investment advisors consists of distinct investment management teams and investment stewardship teams with proxy voting administrative responsibilities. As of the effective date of the Internal Reorganization, VCM and VPM began exercising investment discretion and providing proxy voting administrative services for the funds to which they provide portfolio management services. The U.S. funds for which VGI acts as investment advisor through VCM and VPM (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Investment Committees of the Board of Trustees for the Vanguard-advised funds have adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. The Vanguard Capital Management Investment Stewardship Team and Vanguard Portfolio Management Investment Stewardship Team administer the day-to-day operations of the proxy voting process of the funds managed by VCM and VPM, respectively, as overseen by the relevant Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee appointed by each Investment Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice program are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders under Vanguard's Investor Choice program. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit Proxy voting across Vanguard funds | Vanguard. The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, the voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI, VCM or VPM or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. Votes made by VGI, VCM or VPM, or the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: On January 12, 2026, The Vanguard Group, Inc. ("VGI") and its affiliates (together, "Vanguard") completed an internal reorganization of portfolio management functions for the U.S. Vanguard funds into two wholly owned U.S. investment advisors, Vanguard Capital Management, LLC ("VCM") and Vanguard Portfolio Management, LLC ("VPM") (the "Internal Reorganization"). Each of these investment advisors consists of distinct investment management teams and investment stewardship teams with proxy voting administrative responsibilities. As of the effective date of the Internal Reorganization, VCM and VPM began exercising investment discretion and providing proxy voting administrative services for the funds to which they provide portfolio management services. The U.S. funds for which VGI acts as investment advisor through VCM and VPM (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Investment Committees of the Board of Trustees for the Vanguard-advised funds have adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. The Vanguard Capital Management Investment Stewardship Team and Vanguard Portfolio Management Investment Stewardship Team administer the day-to-day operations of the proxy voting process of the funds managed by VCM and VPM, respectively, as overseen by the relevant Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee appointed by each Investment Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice program are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders under Vanguard's Investor Choice program. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit Proxy voting across Vanguard funds | Vanguard. The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, the voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI, VCM or VPM or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. In addition, votes contained in this report include votes made by unaffiliated third-party investment advisors (External Advisors) who exercised voting power overs some or all of the securities voted. Votes made by VGI, VCM or VPM, or the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: Date of reporting period: July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025 A Fund does not have the right to vote proxies for securities on loans over a record date of such proxies. However, if a Fund's Adviser has notice of the proxy in advance of the record date, the Fund's Adviser may terminate a loan in advance of the record date if the Fund's Adviser determines the vote is considered material with respect to an investment, such as when the Fund's Adviser believes that its participation in the vote is necessary to preserve the long-term value of the Fund's investment or in highly contested issues for which the Fund's Adviser believes its vote is important to the Fund's strategy. In determining whether a vote is material, the Adviser's determination is informed by its responsibility to act in a Fund's best interests. In most cases, the Adviser anticipates that the potential long-term value to a Fund of voting shares would not be material and would therefore not justify forgoing the potential revenue the loan may provide the Fund. This may result in proxies being voted by the borrower of the security in a way that would be contrary to how the Fund's Adviser would vote if the security had not been lent, including for certain Funds that have strategies to invest in companies that the Fund's Adviser believes are sustainable leaders based on the Adviser's sustainability criteria or that meet certain other Environmental, Social, or Governance (ESG) criteria. However, in certain instances, the Adviser may determine, in its independent business judgment, that the value of voting outweighs the securities lending revenue loss to a Fund and may therefore recall shares to be voted in those instances.

 Summary Statement
 Obligation to provide a confidential report has been met and all initial reporting and compliance measures have been taken to comply with the Conflict of Interest Act .
 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist the public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate measure to prevent any opportunity while exercising my official powers, duties and functions to further the private interests of my spouse, Ms. Sophie Grégoire Trudeau, Volunteer of the Canadian Mental Health Association (CMHA) or by giving preferential treatment to CMHA that may have future dealings with the Government of Canada.
This screen is administered by my Chief of Staff and the Clerk of the Privy Council and Secretary to the Cabinet to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor a participant in any discussions or decision-making processes pertaining to the private interests of my spouse or matters relating specifically to the CMHA itself, unless the interest is in a decision or matter that is of general application.
My cabinet and my ministerial staff have been informed in writing of this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner of any additional matters I am made aware of in the future that should form part of the subject matter of this voluntary conflict of interest screen.
In the event that any relevant matter is not caught by the screen and comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Conflict of Interest Act to recuse myself from that issue or matter and inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner.

 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends. 
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my friends, Amaryllis Harrison and Stéphanie Blackett, employed with PAA Advisory or to give preferential treatment to PAA Advisory while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to PAA Advisory. I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. 
I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrator know or reasonably should know to affect my friends’ private interest. 
This screen is administered by the Director of Policy in the Quebec Lieutenant’s Office to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decisions-making processes involving my friends’ private interests, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my friends’ private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.

 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends. 
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder, to further the private interests of my friend, Ms. Beth Palmer, a Senior Consultant at Earnscliffe Strategy, or to give preferential treatment to Earnscliffe Strategy on the basis of this friendship.
Accordingly, I have agreed to abstain from any discussion or decision in relation to Earnscliffe Strategy. I also agree to not have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes affecting my friend or Earnscliffe Strategies.
This screen is administered by my Chief of Staff to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decisions-making processes involving my friend’s private interests, or Earnscliffe Strategy’s private interests, unless the interest in the decision or matter is of general application.
My minister, chief of staff, direct reports, my colleagues and necessary public servants for the purposes of the administration of this screen have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list

 Recusal
 On October 5, 2023, in the exercise of my official duties, I recused myself from any discussion on a bill sponsored by a private Member which would increase the tax benefits for Canada's volunteer firefighters in order to avoid any opportunity to further the private interests of my uncle, a volunteer fire chief in Madeira Park, British Columbia.
 Compliance Order under Section 30
 WHEREAS you are appointed Policy Advisor (PACIFICAN) in the Office of the Minister of International Development and Minister responsible for the Pacific Economic Development Agency of Canada;
WHEREAS pursuant to subsection 28 of the Conflict of Interest Act, I am required to review annually with you, as a reporting public office holder, the information contained in your confidential report and the measures taken to satisfy your obligations under the Act;
WHEREAS an email dated February 18, 2022, was sent to you asking that you return all necessary documents to complete your Annual Review to the Office within 30 days; 
WHEREAS despite many reminders, your Annual Review remains outstanding on the day of this Order; 
AND WHEREAS pursuant to section 19 of the Conflict of Interest Act, compliance with the Act is a condition of a person's appointment or employment as a public office holder;
I THEREFORE ORDER YOU to submit to my Office, within 10 days, all documents identified in the letter dated February 18, 2022, all of which are required to complete your Annual Review.

 Outside Activities
 Notice of Material Change
Date of Change: 2025/07/01
Treasurer of the Knights of Columbus 9544 Council, Holy Redeemer, Kanata, Ontario.
 Recusal
 In the exercise of my official duties as Member of the Veterans Review and Appeal Board , I recused myself on June 12, 2024, from participating in any discussion or decision regarding the revision of a case in order to avoid any appearance of preferential treatment or any opportunity to further the private interest of a friend of mine.
The name of the friend should not be disclosed pursuant to sec. 51 (2) (b) (vi) of the Conflict of Interest which reads as follows:
51 (2) If a public office holder has recused himself or herself in respect of a matter and a public declaration is made in respect of that recusal under subsection 25 (1) or section 30
(b) no publication of the declaration shall include any detail that could reveal, directly or indirectly, any of the following:
(vi) information that could reasonably be expected to cause injury to the privacy interests of an individual.

 Agreed Compliance Measures
 WHEREAS by reason of my appointment on June 3, 2020 as a federal reporting public office holder, I am subject to the Conflict of Interest Act (“Act”), including its prohibition on holding controlled assets (section
17).
WHEREAS I have opted to divest my controlled assets, namely 333 Class “F4” shares in the capital of O.R.M. Ltd., by placing them into a blind trust, in accordance with section 27 of the Act. 
WHEREAS O.R.M. Ltd. (the corporation) is a private holding corporation that holds investments in controlled assets as defined by section 20 of the Act.
AND WHEREAS pursuant to section 29 of the Act, the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner (Commissioner) has determined that the following additional compliance measures are required in order for
me to comply with the requirements of the Act:
1. I shall not instruct, direct or advise the corporation’s directors, officers or shareholders (including the Trustees of the Macklem Family Trust) or anyone else acting on the corporation’s behalf, with respect to the corporation’s controlled assets, including the management, disposition or investment of those assets.
2. I shall refuse all requests for discussion, consultation, instruction, direction or advice by the corporation’s directors, officers, shareholders, or by anyone else acting on the corporation’s behalf, with respect to the corporation’s controlled assets. I will also refuse any information offered to me by the directors, officers, and shareholders of the corporation about the corporation’s controlled assets.
3. Any person or entity, including any director, officer, or shareholder of the corporation who communicates with me in respect of the corporation’s controlled assets shall be directed by me to the Trustee of my blind trust.

 Summary Statement
 Obligation to provide a confidential report has been met and all initial reporting and compliance measures have been taken to comply with the Conflict of Interest Act .
 Agreed Compliance Measures
 In order to prevent a conflict of interest situation from arising between my official duties and my previous employer, the University of Western Ontario from which I am currently on a leave of absence, the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner has determined that a conflict of interest screen is necessary to assist with my obligations under the Conflict of Interest Act to prevent any conflict of interest and in particular to avoid extending preferential treatment to the University of Western Ontario.
Accordingly, a conflict of interest screen has been established and will be administered by my Executive Assistant to ensure that I will abstain from any participation in any discussions or decision-making processes and any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or issue forming part of the subject matter of the conflict of interest screen that is not of general application.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner of all matters of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the subject matter of the conflict of interest screen, in order to prevent a conflict of interest.
In the event that any issue or matter subject to the conflict of interest screen is not caught by that screen and comes before me, I undertake to recuse myself from that issue or matter as required by Section 21 of the Conflict of Interest Act and inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner.
The Deputy Minister of Industry Canada and all employees of the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada have been notified accordingly.

Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holders and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends. 
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further my private interests or to improperly further those of the Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), or its subsidiaries, affiliates and associates, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder.

 Notice of Material Change
Date: 2023-03-25
I am no longer Secretary or board member of the Ottawa South Provincial Liberal Electoral District Association, Ottawa, Ontario
 Past Chair, Equal Voice, National Capital Region Chapter, Ottawa, Ontario
 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity, while I exercise my official powers, duties, and functions as a reporting public office holder, to further the private interests of my friends listed below and avoiding the perception of giving preferential treatment to Earnscliffe Strategies and employer of my friends as well as their clients.
Katie Grandis, Senior Consultant
Alicia Adams, Principal 
Sophie Laghi-Ford, Executive Coordinator
Megan Buttle, Principal
Mary Anne Carter, Principal
Shane O’Neil, Senior Consultant
Emma Macklem, Senior Consultant
Delaney Cullinan, Consultant
Stephanie Constable, Principal
Doug Anderson, Principal
As well as, my friend, Megan Ross an analyst with Abacus Data.
Accordingly, I have agreed to abstain from any discussion or decision in relation to my friends listed above, Earnscliffe Strategies and Abacus Data. I also agree to not have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes involving my friends, Abacus Data, Earncliffe Strategies or their clients.

 Obligation to provide a confidential report has been met and all initial reporting and compliance measures have been taken to comply with the Conflict of Interest Act .
 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends. 
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my friend, Ms. Gail Hamamoto, in Special Olympics Canada or its subsidiaries, affiliates and associates, or to give preferential treatment to Special Olympics Canada, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder. 
Accordingly, I have agreed to abstain from any discussion or decision in relation to Special Olympics Canada or its subsidiaries, affiliates, and associates. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes affecting my friend's interests. 
This screen is administered by the Deputy Minister and my Chief of Staff to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving my friend's private interests, unless the interest in the decision or matter is of general application. Moreover, all authorities for decisions on matters that form part of this screen will be exercised by the Minister of Canadian Heritage.

 Summary Statement
 Obligation to provide a confidential report has been met and all initial reporting and compliance measures have been taken to comply with the Conflict of Interest Act .
 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist them in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends. 
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my father, Mr. Bruce Belbin, in Choices for Youth or its subsidiaries, affiliates and associates, or to give preferential treatment, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder. 
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to Choices for Youth or its subsidiaries, affiliates and associates. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrator know or reasonably should know to affect my father's interests. 
This screen is administered by the Director of Policy to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving my father's private interests, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my father’s interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.

 COMPLIANCE ORDER – PUBLIC OFFICE HOLDER AT THE CANADIAN ENERGY REGULATOR
WHEREAS you were appointed as a Director of the Canadian Energy Regulator pursuant to the Canadian Energy Regulator Act;
WHEREAS, you are also a public office holder subject to the Conflict of Interest Act (Act);
WHEREAS section 4 of the Act sets out the circumstances under which a public office holder is generally understood to be in a conflict of interest for the purposes of the Act, namely when they exercise an official power, duty or function that provides an opportunity to further their private interests, those of their relatives or friends, or to improperly further another person’s private interests;
WHEREAS, the Canadian Energy Regulator Act imposes additional circumstances under which public office holders at the Canadian Energy Regulator are understood to be in a conflict of interest for the purposes of the Act, and they include:
(a) engaging in, as owner, shareholder, director, officer, partner or in any other way, the business of producing, selling, buying, transmitting, exporting, importing or otherwise dealing in hydrocarbons, electricity or offshore energy;
(b) holding any bond, debenture or other security of a corporation engaged in any such business; and
(c) holding other employment that is inconsistent with their powers, duties and functions or with any provision of this Act or a regulation made under it.
WHEREAS I have the authority under paragraph 51(1)(e) to make any document I consider appropriate available for public inspection on the public registry maintained by my Office;
AND WHEREAS, I have determined it necessary, in light of the above, to impose the following compliance measures on you because of your position as a Director at the Canadian Energy Regulator so as to ensure compliance with the Act;
I THEREFORE ORDER YOU pursuant to section 30 of the Act to:
(a) Provide my Office with a confidential disclosure form disclosing all of your investments and activities within 60 days of the date of your appointment;

 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my friends Chad Rogers and Jaime Watt or to give preferential treatment to their respective firms Crestview Strategy and Navigator Ltd. in the exercise of my official powers, duties, and functions as a reporting public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to Crestview Strategy and Navigator Ltd. or their subsidiaries, affiliates, and associates. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making process which I or my administrator know or reasonably should know to affect my friends' private interests
This screen is administered by Tushara Williams, Deputy Secretary to the Cabinet (Operations), Privy Council Office, to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving my friends' private interests, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application.
My colleagues and necessary public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.

 Summary Statement
 Obligation to provide a confidential report has been met and all initial reporting and compliance measures have been taken to comply with the Conflict of Interest Act .
 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist the public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate measure to prevent any opportunity while exercising my official powers, duties and functions to further the private interests of my friend, Ms. Amanda Alvaro, President of Pomp & Circumstance or by giving preferential treatment to Pomp & Circumstance that may have future dealings with the Government of Canada.
This screen is administered by my Chief of Staff to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor a participant in any discussions or decision-making processes pertaining to the private interests of my friend or matters relating specifically to Pomp & Circumstances, unless the interest is in a decision or matter that is of general application.

Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holders and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.

Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to Ms. O’Brien, Barrack Hill Public Affairs and its clients. I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrator knows or reasonably should know to affect my common-law partner’s private interests. 
This screen is administered by the Director of Policy to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving Ms. O’Brien, Barrack Hill Public Affairs and its clients’ private interests.  Public Declaration of Agreed Compliance Measures (Section 29) 
 No Longer Applicable
 Victoria Perak 
 · Policy and Operations Advisor 
 Description 
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist them in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my friend, Ms. Sasha Kardos-Machado, Research Advisor for PAA Advisory, or from giving preferential treatment to PAA Advisory while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to my friend. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrator know or reasonably should know to affect my friend’s private interests. 
This screen is administered by Joshua Mbandi, Director of Policy for the Office of the Secretary of State (Canada Revenue Agency and Financial Institutions), to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decisions-making processes

 Public Declaration of Agreed Compliance Measures (Section 29) 
 No Longer Applicable
 Christina Rettig 
 · Policy Advisor 
 Description 
In order to prevent a conflict of interest situation from arising and to avoid the perception of preferential treatment, the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner has determined that a conflict of interest screen is necessary to assist with my obligation to abstain from participation in any matters, other than those of general application, on which my spouse, Mr. Damien O’Brien, Senior Public Affairs Consultant with Edelman, makes representations on behalf of clients. 
Accordingly, a conflict of interest screen has been established and will be administered by the Director of Policy in the Office of the Prime Minister to ensure that I will abstain from any participation in any discussions or decision-making processes and any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or issue forming part of the subject matter of the conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner of all matters of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the subject matter of the conflict of interest screen, in order to prevent a conflict of interest.
In the event that any issue or matter subject to the conflict of interest screen is not caught by that screen and comes before me, I undertake to recuse myself from that issue or matter as required by Section 21 of the Conflict of Interest Act and inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner.
The Prime Minister and all ministerial staff

 Public Declaration of Agreed Compliance Measures (Section 29) 
 No Longer Applicable
 Arianne Reza 
 · Deputy Minister 
 Description 
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures that are agreed upon by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act), to assist the public office holder in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of public office holders and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me in order to avoid the appearance of preferential treatment or any opportunity to further the private interests of my relative, Kayvan Lira, or to give preferential treatment to his employer Databricks or its subsidiaries, affiliates and associates, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to pre-emptively recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to Kayvan Lira and his employer Databricks. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes affecting my relative’s interests.
This screen is administered by my Chief of Staff and Deputy Minister of Employment and Social Development Canada, Paul Thompson, to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making process

 Description 
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends. 
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder, to further the private interests of a family friend, Richard Quintal, CEO and Chief of Staff to the President of Metis Nation of Saskatchewan (MN-S) and my friend Ms. Jessica Hayden, Associate Director of The Early Years Program at the Martin Family Initiative (MFI). The screen will also prevent giving any preferential treatment to MN-S and MFI on the basis of the identity of Mr. Quintal and Ms. Hayden.

 COMPLIANCE ORDER – REPORTING PUBLIC OFFICE HOLDER AT THE CANADIAN ENERGY REGULATOR
WHEREAS you were appointed as a Commissioner of the Canadian Energy Regulator pursuant to the Canadian Energy Regulator Act;
WHEREAS, you are also a reporting public office holder subject to the Conflict of Interest Act (Act);
WHEREAS section 4 of the Act sets out the circumstances under which a public office holder is generally understood to be in a conflict of interest for the purposes of the Act, namely when they exercise an official power, duty or function that provides an opportunity to further their private interests, those of their relatives or friends, or to improperly further another person’s private interests;
WHEREAS, the Canadian Energy Regulator Act imposes additional circumstances under which public office holders at the Canadian Energy Regulator are understood to be in a conflict of interest for the purposes of the Act, and they include: 
(a) engaging in, as owner, shareholder, director, officer, partner or in any other way, the business of producing, selling, buying, transmitting, exporting, importing or otherwise dealing in hydrocarbons, electricity or offshore energy;
(b) holding any bond, debenture or other security of a corporation engaged in any such business; and
(c) holding other employment that is inconsistent with their powers, duties and functions or with any provision of this Act or a regulation made under it.

 Summary Statement
 Obligation to provide a confidential report has been met and all initial reporting and compliance measures have been taken to comply with the Conflict of Interest Act .
 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist the public office holder in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Interim Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder, to further the private interests of my friend, Viveka Melki, founder and owner of Melki Films, or to give preferential treatment to Melki Films on the basis of my friendship.
Accordingly, I have agreed to abstain from any discussion, decision, debate, or vote in relation to Melki Films. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes affecting the interests of my friend or Melki Films. This screen is co-administered by my Executive Assistant and the Corporate Secretary to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving the private interest of my friend or Melki Films unless the interest in the decision or matter is of general application.
The Minister of Canadian Heritage, the Museum’s Board of Trustees, the members of my staff and all other necessary colleagues and public servants for the purposes of the administration of this screen have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.

 Agreed Compliance Measures
 (This declaration replaces the one published on May 17, 2023.)
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by public office holders and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist them in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holders and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends. 
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the interests of Université de Montréal or to give preferential treatment to this organization, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself, in my capacity as a public office holder, from any discussion or decision in relation to Université de Montréal. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrators know or reasonably should know to affect the interests of Université de Montreal.
This screen is co-administered by the Executive Vice-President and the Vice-President, Research - Programs of the Canadian Institutes of Health Research (CIHR) to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decisions-making processes involving the interests of Université de Montréal. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect the interests of Université de Montréal as a member of a broad class of organizations unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class. 
The Minister of Health as well as the members of the Governing Council, the Executive Management, the Scientific Directors and staff members of the CIHR have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.

 On June 30, 2020, in the exercise of my official duties, I recused myself from participating in a communication in order to avoid any conflict of interest between my official functions and the private interests of my relative, who is an employee of the Manitoba Keewatinowi Okimakanak Inc.

 Compliance Order under Section 30
 WHEREAS you are appointed Director of Labour Relations in the Office of the President of the Treasury Board; 
WHEREAS pursuant to subsection 28 of the Conflict of Interest Act, I am required to review annually with you, as a reporting public office holder, the information contained in your confidential report and the measures taken to satisfy your obligations under the Act; 
WHEREAS an email dated May 24, 2022, was sent to you asking that you return all necessary documents to complete your Annual Review to the Office within 30 days; 
WHEREAS despite many reminders, your Annual Review remains outstanding on the day of this Order; 
AND WHEREAS pursuant to section 19 of the Conflict of Interest Act, compliance with the Act is a condition of a person's appointment or employment as a public office holder; 
I THEREFORE ORDER YOU to submit to my Office, within 10 days of the deemed date of service of this order, all documents identified in the letter dated May 24, 2022, all of which are required to complete your Annual Review.
