 Summary Statement
 Obligation to provide a confidential report has been met and all initial reporting and compliance measures have been taken to comply with the Conflict of Interest Act .
 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends. 
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my friend employed by the Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs (CIJA), or to give preferential treatment to CIJA, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to CIJA. I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrators know or reasonably should know to affect my friend’s private interests. 
This screen is administered by the Director of Quebec, Francophone and Legal Affairs to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decisions-making processes involving my friend’s private interests, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my friend’s private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.

 Summary Statement
 Obligation to provide a confidential report has been met and all initial reporting and compliance measures have been taken to comply with the Conflict of Interest Act .
 Assets
 Rental property joint with an individual, located in Toronto, Ontario
 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends. 
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my spouse, Ms. Janice Nicholson, Vice-President, Digital at Bluesky Strategy Group, or to give preferential treatment to Bluesky Strategy Group, as a reporting public office holder. 
Accordingly, I have agreed to abstain from any discussion or decision in relation to Bluesky Strategy Group. I also agree to not have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes affecting Bluesky Strategy Group. 
This screen is administered by the Director of Policy in the Office of the Prime Minister to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decisions-making processes involving my spouse’s private interests, or the Bluesky Strategy Group’s private interests, unless the interest in the decision or matter is of general application. 
The Prime Minister, chief of staff, colleagues and necessary public servants have all been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen. 
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.

 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my partner, Mr. Sébastien Fassier, Vice-President, TACT or to give preferential treatment to TACT as a reporting public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to abstain from any discussion or decision in relation to TACT. I also agree to not have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes affecting my partner’s private interests.
This screen is administered by the Director of Regional Affairs in the office of the Québec Lieutenant to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decisions-making processes involving my spouse private interests, or the TACT’s private interests, unless the interest in the decision or matter is of general application.

 COMPLIANCE ORDER – PUBLIC OFFICE HOLDER AT THE CANADIAN ENERGY REGULATOR
WHEREAS you were appointed as a Director of the Canadian Energy Regulator pursuant to the Canadian Energy Regulator Act;
WHEREAS, you are also a public office holder subject to the Conflict of Interest Act (Act);
WHEREAS section 4 of the Act sets out the circumstances under which a public office holder is generally understood to be in a conflict of interest for the purposes of the Act, namely when they exercise an official power, duty or function that provides an opportunity to further their private interests, those of their relatives or friends, or to improperly further another person’s private interests;
WHEREAS, the Canadian Energy Regulator Act imposes additional circumstances under which public office holders at the Canadian Energy Regulator are understood to be in a conflict of interest for the purposes of the Act, and they include:
(a) engaging in, as owner, shareholder, director, officer, partner or in any other way, the business of producing, selling, buying, transmitting, exporting, importing or otherwise dealing in hydrocarbons, electricity or offshore energy;
(b) holding any bond, debenture or other security of a corporation engaged in any such business; and
(c) holding other employment that is inconsistent with their powers, duties and functions or with any provision of this Act or a regulation made under it.
WHEREAS I have the authority under paragraph 51(1)(e) to make any document I consider appropriate available for public inspection on the public registry maintained by my Office;

 Obligation to provide a confidential report has been met and all initial reporting and compliance measures have been taken to comply with the Conflict of Interest Act .
 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends. 
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my spouse, Mr. Maximilien Roy, Vice President, Federal and Quebec, of Restaurants Canada, or to improperly further the private interest of, or give preferential treatment to Restaurants Canada, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder. 
Accordingly, I have agreed to abstain from any discussion or decision in relation to Restaurants Canada or its subsidiaries, affiliates, and associates. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes affecting my spouse's or Restaurants Canada’s private interests.
This screen is administered by the Chief of Staff of the Minister of Small Business with the assistance of my Director of Policy to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving my spouse’s private interests, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. 
My minister, direct reports, colleagues and necessary public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.

 Examination Report
 This report presents the findings of my examination under the Conflict of Interest Act of the conduct of Ms. Marie Chapman, Chief Executive Officer of the Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21, a federal Crown corporation.
As a result of a disclosure referred to my Office in October 2017 by the Office of the Public Sector Integrity Commissioner, my predecessor launched an examination on her own initiative in order to determine whether Ms. Chapman contravened subsection 6(1) and section 21 of the Act when she offered Ms. Jennifer Sutherland, an alleged friend, a contract for a term position in 2014, and appointed her to a permanent position in 2015.

 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends. 
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my friends Olivia Neil, director at Microsoft, Imraan Bashir, partner at KPMG and Matej Pivac, director, consulting expert at CGI, or to give preferential treatment to them while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to abstain from any discussion or decision in relation to any procurement process that could involve my friends or their employers. I also agree to not have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes affecting my friend’s interests.

Moreover, all powers, duties and functions on matters that form part of this screen will be exercised by the Associate Deputy Minister of Public Services and Procurement Canada.

AND WHEREAS pursuant to section 19 of the Conflict of Interest Act, compliance with the Act is a condition of a person's appointment or employment as a public office holder;

 Assets
 Sole ownership of a rental property located in Richmond, British Columbia
 Waiver Granted Pursuant to Section 39
 In accordance with section 39 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act), Ms. Annette Anselm, former Member of the Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada (IRB), has been granted a waiver of her limitation period under section 36 insofar as it relates to entering into a contract of service with the IRB.
Ms. Anselm applied for a waiver of the period that applies to former reporting public office holders for one year following the last day in office. The waiver of the limitation period allows Ms. Anselm to enter into a contract of service with the IRB. 
In reviewing Ms. Anselm’s request, I considered all relevant factors listed under subsection 39(3) of the Act, which includes the following:
The general employment prospects of the reporting public office holder or former reporting public office holder
- Ms. Anselm has a specialty in the area which is very specific to the administration of refugee law. 
The nature and significance to the Government of Canada of the information possessed by the former reporting public office holder by virtue of that office holder’s public office
- Ms. Anselm has earned knowledge during her mandate that will continue to benefit the IRB. 
In light of the above, I have determined that the public interest in granting the waiver in relation to a contract of service to Ms. Anselm with the IRB outweighs the public interest in maintaining the prohibition. I have therefore agreed to waive the limitation period for this contract.
All other post-employment obligations under the Act continue to apply, including the prohibition on contracting or accepting employment or an appointment to a board position with any other entity set out in subsection 35(1) as well as the prohibition on making any other representations within the meaning of subsection 35(2), for the remainder of Ms. Anselm’s limitation period.

 Obligation to provide a confidential report has been met and all initial reporting and compliance measures have been taken to comply with the Conflict of Interest Act .
 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by public office holders and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist them in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holders and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my friend, Philip Baldwin, Vice-President, Government and Public Affairs of the Aerospace Industries Association of Canada (AIAC), or to give preferential treatment to the AIAC, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder. 
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to the AIAC. I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrator know or reasonably should know to affect my friend’s private interests.
This screen is administered by the Director of Policy and Operations to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving my friend’s private interests. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my friend’s private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.

 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my friend, Ms. Ashley Bodiguel, Manager, Operations & Records at Pembina Institute, or to give preferential treatment to Pembina Institute, while I exercise my official powers, duties, and functions as a reporting public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to abstain from any discussion or decision in relation to Pembina Institute. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes affecting Pembina Institute.
This screen is administered by the Chief of Staff to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving Pembina Institute’s private interests, unless the interest in the decision or matter is of general application. 
My minister, colleagues, and necessary public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.

 Agreed Compliance Measures
 WHEREAS by reason of my appointment on July 15, 2020 as a federal reporting public office holder, I am subject to the Conflict of Interest Act (“Act”), including its prohibition on holding controlled assets (section 17). 
WHEREAS I have opted to divest my controlled assets, shares of 173217 Canada Inc. and my shares of 4381831 Canada Inc by placing them into a blind trust, in accordance with section 27 of the Act. 
WHEREAS 173217 Canada Inc. and 4381831 Canada Inc. (the corporations) are a private holding corporations that hold investments in controlled assets as defined by section 20 of the Act. 
AND WHEREAS pursuant to section 29 of the Act, the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner (Commissioner) has determined that the following additional compliance measures are required in order for me to comply with the requirements of the Act:
1. I shall not instruct, direct or advise the corporations’ directors, officers or shareholders or anyone else acting on the corporations’ behalf, with respect to the corporations’ controlled assets, including the management, disposition or investment of those assets. 
2. I shall refuse all requests for discussion, consultation, instruction, direction or advice by the corporations’ directors, officers, shareholders, or by anyone else acting on the corporations’ behalf, with respect to the corporation’s controlled assets. I will also refuse any information offered to me by the directors, officers, and shareholders of the corporation about the corporations’ controlled assets.
3. Any person or entity, including any director, officer, or shareholder of the corporation who communicates with me in respect of the corporations’ controlled assets shall be directed by me to the Trustee of my blind trust.

 Summary Statement
 Obligation to provide a confidential report has been met and all initial reporting and compliance measures have been taken to comply with the Conflict of Interest Act .
 Exemption Granted Pursuant to Section 38
 In accordance with section 38 of the Conflict of Interest Act (the Act), Melanie Thibodeau, former Special Assistant, Regional Affairs at the Office of the Deputy Prime Minister, has been granted an exemption from their post-employment obligations under sections 35 and 37, insofar as it relates to accepting employment with the constituency office of Ginette Petitpas Taylor.
Ms. Thibodeau applied for the exemption from the application of post-employment obligations under sections 35 and 37 of the Act for a former reporting public office holder who was a member of ministerial staff who worked on average 15 hours or more a week. 
The exemption allows Ms. Thibodeau to accept employment with the constituency office of Ginette Petitpas Taylor. It also allows them to make representations on behalf of constituents to federal entities with which they had direct and significant official dealings during the period of one year immediately before their last day in office, to the extent that these representations are in relation to their duties and functions as an employee of the constituency office. 
In reviewing Ms. Thibodeau’s request, I considered all criteria listed under subsection 38(2) of the Act, which include the following:
a) the person was not a senior member of ministerial staff 
b) the person’s functions did not include the handling of files of a political or sensitive 
nature, such as confidential cabinet documents
c) the person had little influence, visibility or decision-making power in the office of a minister of the Crown or a minister of state
d) the person’s salary level was not commensurate with the person having an important role in that office
In light of the above, I have agreed to exempt Ms. Thibodeau of the post-employment obligations under sections 35 and 37 of the Act to allow them to engage in employment with the constituency office of Ginette Petitpas Taylor.

 COMPLIANCE ORDER – REPORTING PUBLIC OFFICE HOLDER AT THE CANADIAN ENERGY REGULATOR
WHEREAS you were appointed as a Commissioner of the Canadian Energy Regulator pursuant to the Canadian Energy Regulator Act;
WHEREAS, you are also a reporting public office holder subject to the Conflict of Interest Act (Act);
WHEREAS section 4 of the Act sets out the circumstances under which a public office holder is generally understood to be in a conflict of interest for the purposes of the Act, namely when they exercise an official power, duty or function that provides an opportunity to further their private interests, those of their relatives or friends, or to improperly further another person’s private interests;
WHEREAS, the Canadian Energy Regulator Act imposes additional circumstances under which public office holders at the Canadian Energy Regulator are understood to be in a conflict of interest for the purposes of the Act, and they include: 
(a) engaging in, as owner, shareholder, director, officer, partner or in any other way, the business of producing, selling, buying, transmitting, exporting, importing or otherwise dealing in hydrocarbons, electricity or offshore energy;
(b) holding any bond, debenture or other security of a corporation engaged in any such business; and
(c) holding other employment that is inconsistent with their powers, duties and functions or with any provision of this Act or a regulation made under it. 
(d) holding office as the Chief Executive Officer or being employed by the Regulator.
WHEREAS I have the authority under paragraph 51(1)(e) to make any document I consider appropriate available for public inspection on the public registry maintained by my Office;

 Summary Statement
 Obligation to provide a confidential report has been met and all initial reporting and compliance measures have been taken to comply with the Conflict of Interest Act .
 Assets
 Joint ownership with spouse of Red Coat Cattle Station, which includes commercial farm land, equipment, crops and livestock, located in Ogema, Saskatchewan
 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Section 15 of the Conflict of Interest Act prohibits a reporting public office holder from managing or operating a commercial activity as well as being an active partner in a partnership. 
I, Lonny McKague, partner of Red Coat Cattle Station, a joint partnership with my spouse, am undertaking to become and remain an inactive partner of this partnership for as long as I am a reporting public office holder subject to the Conflict of Interest Act.
Accordingly, I will not be involved directly or indirectly in the daily management or operations of Red Coat Cattle Station. As a result, my spouse will be solely responsible for all activities of the partnership that would fall within the prohibitions of the Conflict of Interest Act.
This undertaking does not prevent me from performing any non-commercial activities on the premises of Red Coat Cattle Station.
I will also contact the Office of the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner if I have any doubts about activities that may tantamount to the management or operation of a commercial activity.

 Summary Statement
 Obligation to provide a confidential report has been met and all initial reporting and compliance measures have been taken to comply with the Conflict of Interest Act .
 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends. 
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder, to further the private interests of my relative, Don Moors, Partner with Partner of Temple Scott Associates or to give preferential treatment to Temple Scott Associates on the basis of the identity of Mr. Moors. 
Accordingly, I have agreed to abstain from any discussion, decision, debate or vote in relation to Temple Scott Associates. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes involving my relative’s interests.
This screen is administered by the Associate Secretary of the Treasury Board to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decisions-making processes involving my relative’s private interests, unless their interest in the decision or matter is of general application. 
The President of the Treasury Board, the Privy Council Office, the Prime Minister’s Office, direct reports, the members of my staff and all other necessary colleagues and public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.

 COMPLIANCE ORDER- PUBLIC OFFICE HOLDER AT THE CANADA ENERGY REGULATOR 
WHEREAS you were appointed on a part-time basis as a Director of the Canada Energy Regulator pursuant to the Canadian Energy Regulator Act and as such you are a public office holder subject to the Conflict of Interest Act (Act); 
WHEREAS section 4 of the Act sets out the circumstances under which a public office holder is generally understood to be in a conflict of interest for the purposes of the Act, namely when they exercise an official power, duty or function that provides an opportunity to further their private interests, those of their relatives or friends, or to improperly further another person's private interests; 
WHEREAS, the Canadian Energy Regulator Act imposes additional circumstances under which public office holders at the Canada Energy Regulator are understood to be in a conflict of interest for the purposes of the Act, and they include: 
(a) engaging in, as owner, shareholder, director, officer, partner or in any other way, the business of producing, selling, buying, transmitting, exporting, importing or otherwise dealing in hydrocarbons, electricity or offshore energy; 
(b) holding any bond, debenture or other security of a corporation engaged in any such business; and 
(c) holding other employment that is inconsistent with their powers, duties and functions or with any provision of this Act or a regulation made under it. 
WHEREAS the Act does not provide for the necessary measures to address the conflicts of interests for public office holders as contemplated in the Canadian Energy Regulator Act; 
WHEREAS section 30 of the Act provides the Commissioner with the additional authority to order specific measures not contemplated in the Act; 
WHEREAS the Commissioner has the authority under paragraph 51(1)(e) to make any document the Commissioner considers appropriate available for public inspection on the public registry maintained by my Office;

 In accordance with section 39 of the Conflict of Interest Act, Ms. Scieur-Aparicio, former Director of Communications in the Office of the Minister of National Revenue, has been granted a reduction of her limitation period under section 36 to permit her to accept employment with Affaires Politiques, a public relations firm. 
Ms. Scieur-Aparicio applied for a reduction of the period that applies to former reporting public office holders for one year following their last day in office. The reduction allows Ms. Scieur-Aparicio to accept a employment with Affaires Politiques. In reviewing Ms. Scieur-Aparicio’s request, I considered all relevant factors listed under subsection 39(3) of the Act, which include the following: 
- Circumstances of departure: Ms. Scieur-Aparicio departed public office after less than two months.
- General employment prospects: Ms. Scieur-Aparicio’s employment prospects are limited given her expertise and region of residence.
- Degree to which the new employer might gain unfair commercial advantage: No unfair advantage is envisaged since the duration in the position was very short and Ms. Scieur-Aparicio had no influence on the development of policies.
In light of the above, I have determined that the public interest in granting the reduction in relation to Ms. Scieur-Aparicio’s employment with Affaires Politiques outweighs the public interest in maintaining the prohibition. I have therefore waived the limitation period. 
All other post‐employment obligations under the Act continue to apply, including the prohibition on contracting or accepting employment or an appointment to a board position with any other entity set out in subsection 35(1) as well as the prohibition on making representations within the meaning of subsection 35(2), for the duration of Ms. Scieur-Aparicio’s limitation period.

 Agreed Compliance Measures
 Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends. 
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my spouse employed with the United Food and Commercial Workers union (UFCW Canada) or to give preferential treatment to UFCW Canada while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to UFCW Canada. I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. 
I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrators know or reasonably should know to affect my spouse’s private interest. 
This screen is administered by the President and the Registrar of the Canada Industrial Relations Board to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decisions-making processes involving my spouse’s private interests, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my spouse’s private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class. 
The members of the staff of the Canada Industrial Relations Board and my colleagues have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.
